name: apple-glass-controls
about: Web re-creation of the two Liquid Glass control animations on Apple's 'Adopting Liquid Glass' page (Controls section): the slider thumb and the segmented control. Every number was MEASURED frame by frame from Apple's two demo videos (30 fps, 1080 px wide) by extracting the lens bounding box, its rim, area, centre and shape per frame, then fitting a web render (analysis-by-synthesis). Only numbers are stored - no Apple frames or artwork. All lengths are CSS px = video px / 2, i.e. the demo runs at the video's own scale; multiply by `scale` (--gc-scale) for other sizes.

tags.MEASURED: read straight from the video frames
tags.FIT: parameters of a model fitted to measured frames (error noted)
tags.CONV: our convention - the video does not show it

rest.notes: Opaque pill that hides the track; the thumb is 1.46 : 1.

lens.areaNotes: w*h of the pressed lens (incl. rim): 5266 css px^2 when the thumb is still (177x119 video px / 4), ~5030 while it is being dragged (video mean 20127 +- 238 px^2 over frames 14-160). The kit uses 5270: only the aspect changes with motion, not the area. The lens centre sits 1.5 px above the track centre (0.75 px for the rest pill).

aspectLaw.notes: asp = base + gain * tanh(a / accelScale). a = d/dt of the thumb's LOW-PASSED velocity (first-order, velocityTau) in css px/s^2; the aspect then follows this target with a first-order lag (responseTau). Wide (up to ~1.9) while the thumb accelerates to the right or brakes while moving left, tall (down to ~1.1) in the opposite cases - the glass 'sloshes' with inertia. Fitted on 146 frames of drag: rmse 0.069 in aspect. (Velocity alone fits worse: R2 0.45, rmse 0.14.)

veil.notes: grey levels (0-255) of the lens body from its top edge down; 'above'/'below' = just above / below the track band inside the lens

shadow.notes: blue-tinted, offset down: the glass throws the slider colour onto the surface

rim.notes: angular colour of the 1 px rim: electric blue at the left/lower-left, white at the bottom and right

refraction.notes: inward displacement of what is under the lens, largest at the rim (21 px) falling linearly to 0 at 7 px inside; per-channel strength (R,G,B) gives the coloured fringe; produces the blue crescent + horn shapes where the fill meets the rim

glow.notes: soft cyan-white glow just inside the rim (the 'caustic' streaks that curl along the inside of the left cap in the video); strongest at the left (262 deg)

press.notes: progress p (0 = rest pill, 1 = pressed lens), one sample per frame (1/30 s) after the first frame that shows growth. Front-loaded ease: 0.10, 0.36, 0.62, 0.90, 0.97, 1 (a smoothstep over 5.5 frames misses by up to 0.08, so the kit uses the table). The lens area and aspect interpolate with p. Total 0.18 s.

crossfade.notes: opacity of the opaque rest pill laid over the glass, as a function of press progress p. Pressing: it is gone by p = 0.36 (frame 11). Releasing: it comes back LATER than it left - at p = 0.44 the glass still shows through a 60 % rest fill (video frames 166-170) - so the release uses its own curve. Blur (px) of the glass content while it crossfades.

release.notes: progress p after finger-up, per frame. Never overshoots (unlike the segmented control). Three observed releases (area-based) took 3-8 frames; the kit uses their mean. The glass crossfades back to the opaque rest pill while p < 0.35.

track.fillFromValue: the blue fill ends at value*trackWidth
track.notes: video: fill tip = 1.0869*cx - 47.0 video px (residual 0.57 px over 142 frames), i.e. a pure static mapping - the thumb centre travels 19.4 px inside each end of the 476.5 px track, no lag between thumb and fill. Track x 28.5-505 px, thickness 12.5.

drag.notes: The thumb centre is a straight function of the value (no spring lag between pointer, fill and thumb); only the lens SHAPE has inertia (aspectLaw).

track.notes: video: x 142-856, y 88-241 (154 px tall at 2x)

segments.notes: the two segments are content-sized, not equal: pill centres at 96.5 and 275.25 px from the track's left edge, pill widths 189 ('For You') and 159.5 ('Library'), measured incl. rim; 2.5 px inset from the track, 4 px between pills. Other segment counts: equal split (CONV)

pill.widthSwitchNotes: the pill/lens width changes from one segment's width to the next only in the last 45 % of the travel (video: 209 -> 203 -> 187 -> 171 -> 155 css over the last 5 frames); before that it keeps the old segment's width

label.notes: Measured in the video: cap height 20 css px, text width 95 css px ('For You') and 85 ('Library') = ratio 1.118. SF Pro Semibold gives that at ~26 px (width 3.7 em); Arial/Helvetica Bold at 26.5 px gives 97/89 px, so the kit sizes labels 26.5 px with the Apple system font first and Helvetica/Arial as the fallback (DejaVu/Inter are ~14 % wider - do not use them here). Selected label black, unselected rgba(0,0,0,.373) (=#838383 on the track).

lens.notes: the pressed lens is the current segment pill grown by 22.5 css px in width and 28.5 in height (For You 189 -> 211.5 x 75 -> 103; Library 159.5 -> 182 x 75 -> 103). It is TALLER than the track (103 vs 77): it pops out above and below.
lens.magnificationNotes: label glyphs inside the lens are 1.15x (219 vs 190 video px for 'For You'); the lens shows the selected-state (black) copy of BOTH labels, so unselected labels turn black under it

material.veilNotes: grey level at fraction of lens height from the top (measured at the lens centre, frame 15)

refraction.notes: same bevel as the slider; visible as the smeared glyph edges (For Yo|u, Libra|ry)

press.notes: progress p per frame from the first growth frame. Height first: pill 150 -> 206 (video px 149 -> 206 for For You). The glass (bright veil, refraction) switches on between samples 4 and 5 (one frame); before that the pill just grows.

transit.notes: tap on the other segment: the lens centre moves with an under-damped spring (omega 6.8 rad/s, zeta 0.72, rmse 0.034 of the distance) starting 7 frames after the press; slower drags fit omega ~4.1 (follows the pointer). Overshoots ~2 %. Delay 0.29 s (8 frames incl. the sampling convention) after finger-down.

release.notes: progress p after release, per frame: it falls through 0 in ~5 frames, UNDERSHOOTS to -0.18 (the pill shrinks 10 video px below its rest size), overshoots +0.07 and settles by ~0.65 s. Half period 7 frames = 0.23 s. Measured in three separate releases (undershoot -0.18, -0.07, -0.19). Tap on the other segment (video 1): the finger is up after ~7 frames but the lens keeps its size while it travels - it droops 0.03/frame (0.9/s, floor 0.75) and the shrink starts when 70 % of the distance is covered (frame 24, p 0.68).

reducedMotion.rule: Under prefers-reduced-motion: no growth, no stretch, no spring; the selected pill moves with a 0.15 s crossfade, the slider thumb stays the rest pill.
